sections.title: Nuclear Radioactivity
objectives: Explain the types of radiation—alpha emission, beta emission, and gamma emission.
Explain the ionization of radiation in an atom.

misconceptions.claim: The half life of a radioactive sample is a fixed time.
misconceptions.correction: It is a fixed proportion. Half of whatever is left decays in each half life, whatever the amount.

summary: Some nuclei are radioactive—they spontaneously decay destroying some part of their mass and emitting energetic rays, a process called nuclear radioactivity.
Nuclear radiation, like x rays, is ionizing radiation, because energy sufficient to ionize matter is emitted in each decay.

The range (or distance traveled in a material) of ionizing radiation is directly related to the charge of the emitted particle and its energy, with greater-charge and lower-energy particles having the shortest ranges.

sections.title: Radiation Detection and Detectors
objectives: Explain the working principle of a Geiger tube.
summary: Radiation detectors are based directly or indirectly upon the ionization created by radiation, as are the effects of radiation on living and inert materials.
Explain nuclear radiation.

sections.title: Substructure of the Nucleus
objectives: Define and discuss the nucleus in an atom.
Calculate the density of the nucleus.

misconceptions.claim: The activity of a sample depends on the mass of the sample.
misconceptions.correction: It depends on how many nuclei are left, so a larger sample is more active even though the half life is the same.

summary: Two particles, both called nucleons, are found inside nuclei. The two types of nucleons are protons and neutrons; they are very similar, except that the proton is positively charged while the neutron is neutral. Some of their characteristics are given in and compared with those of the electron. A mass unit convenient to atomic and nuclear processes is the unified atomic mass unit (u), defined to be 1 u = 1.6605 × 10 − 27 kg = 931.46 MeV / c 2 .

A nuclide is a specific combination of protons and neutrons, denoted by ZAXN or simplyAX,Z is the number of protons or atomic number, X is the symbol for the element, N is the number of neutrons, and A is the mass number or the total number of protons and neutrons, A=N+Z.
Nuclides having the same Z but different N are isotopes of the same element.

sections.title: Nuclear Decay and Conservation Laws
objectives: Calculate the energy emitted during nuclear decay.
summary: When a parent nucleus decays, it produces a daughter nucleus following rules and conservation laws. There are three major types of nuclear decay, called alpha α, beta β, and gamma γ. The α decay equation is ZAXN→Z−2A−4YN−2+24He2.
Nuclear decay releases an amount of energy E related to the mass destroyed Δm byE=(Δm)c2.
There are three forms of beta decay. The β−decay equation is ZAXN→Z+1AYN−1+β−+ν¯e.

sections.title: Half-Life and Activity
objectives: Calculate age of old objects by radioactive dating.
summary: Half-life t1/2 is the time in which there is a 50% chance that a nucleus will decay. The number of nuclei N as a function of time isN=N0e−λt, where N0 is the number present at t=0, and λ is the decay constant, related to the half-life by λ=0.693t1/2.

One of the applications of radioactive decay is radioactive dating, in which the age of a material is determined by the amount of radioactive decay that occurs. The rate of decay is called the activity R:R= Δ N Δ t .
The SI unit for R is the becquerel (Bq), defined by 1 Bq=1 decay/s.

sections.title: Binding Energy
objectives: Calculate the binding energy per nucleon of a particle.
summary: The binding energy (BE) of a nucleus is the energy needed to separate it into individual protons and neutrons. In terms of atomic masses, BE={[Zm(1H)+Nmn]−m(AX)}c2, where m1H is the mass of a hydrogen atom, mAX is the atomic mass of the nuclide, and mn is the mass of a neutron. Patterns in the binding energy per nucleon, BE/A, reveal details of the nuclear force. The larger the BE/A, the more stable the nucleus.

sections.title: Tunneling
summary: Tunneling is a quantum mechanical process of potential energy barrier penetration. The concept was first applied to explain α decay, but tunneling is found to occur in other quantum mechanical systems.
Explain nuclear radiation.
Explain the types of radiation—alpha emission, beta emission, and gamma emission.

exam_traps.misconception: The half life of a radioactive sample is a fixed time.
exam_traps.correction: It is a fixed proportion. Half of whatever is left decays in each half life, whatever the amount.
exam_traps.signal: Our own teaching of the section, waiting for a paper question that shows the same mistake.

exam_traps.subject: physics
exam_traps.misconception: The activity of a sample depends on the mass of the sample.
exam_traps.correction: It depends on how many nuclei are left, so a larger sample is more active even though the half life is the same.
exam_traps.signal: Our own teaching of the section, waiting for a paper question that shows the same mistake.

exam_traps.subject: physics
exam_traps.misconception: The half-life of a radioactive sample is the time in which all of it decays.
exam_traps.correction: It is the time in which half the nuclei decay. The sample never decays completely in a finite time, and the same half-life applies however much you start with.
exam_traps.signal: Our own question offers the full decay as an option.

exam_traps.subject: physics
exam_traps.misconception: In alpha decay the nucleus emits an electron.
exam_traps.correction: It emits a helium nucleus, made of two protons and two neutrons, and the atomic number falls by two. The electron is the beta particle, emitted in beta decay instead.
exam_traps.signal: Our own question offers the electron as an option.

exam_recall_checks.stem: The half-life of a radioactive sample is

options.text: the time for all of it to decay
the time for half of it to decay
the time for its mass to halve by any route
the time for the activity to reach zero

exam_recall_checks.explanation: The half-life is the time in which half the nuclei decay. The mass also halves in that time, but the definition is in terms of the nuclei.
